item.title: Azure Cosmos DB
item.author: emecas
item.description:
Azure Cosmos DB
https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/cosmos-db/#overview
Build or modernize scalable, high-performance apps

Azure Cosmos DB is a fully managed, serverless NoSQL database for high-performance applications of any size or scale. Get guaranteed single-digit millisecond performance and 99.999-percent availability, backed by SLAs, automatic and instant scalability, enterprise-grade security, and open-source APIs for NoSQL databases including MongoDB and Cassandra. Enjoy fast writes and reads anywhere in the world with multi-region writes and data replication. Gain insight over real-time data with no-ETL (extract, transform, load) analytics using Azure Synapse Link for Azure Cosmos DB.

item.title: Deno
item.author: emecas
item.description:
Deno
https://deno.land
https://deno.town
https://github.com/denoland/deno

https://github.com/architect/architect

Deno is a brand new experimental JavaScript runtime and deno.town is a web based REPL with linting and code completion to help you explore and learn the API.
Why Deno?

It is very fast
Built in least privilege security
Standard esmodules
TypeScript, JSX and TSX dialects supported

How

AWS Lambda (and friends) by way of OpenJS Architect
Deployed continuously with begin.com (Note! We have not officially released Deno support. Keep reading if you are interested in that.)

item.title: Serverless Architectures
item.author: emecas
item.description:
Serverless Architectures
https://www.martinfowler.com/articles/serverless.html
By Mike Roberts
Serverless architectures refer to applications that significantly depend on third-party services (knows as Backend as a Service or “BaaS”) or on custom code that’s run in ephemeral containers (Function as a Service or “FaaS”), the best known vendor host of which currently is AWS Lambda. By using these ideas, and by moving much behavior to the front end, such architectures remove the need for the traditional ‘always on’ server system sitting behind an application. Depending on the circumstances, such systems can significantly reduce operational cost and complexity at a cost of vendor dependencies and (at the moment) immaturity of supporting services.
